excerpt: Compare the cash flow, flexibility and five-year costs of buying or renting an apartment in Ajman.
introduction:
Buying an apartment in Ajman may suit a household that expects to stay, can afford the complete purchase and wants control over its home. Renting may suit someone who values flexibility or wants to keep capital available. The financial answer depends on the specific apartment, length of stay, purchase costs, rent, finance and what happens when the owner sells.

Compare two homes that meet the same needs and use the same time horizon. The worked example below shows how a household can compare purchase and rental costs over the same period.
takeaways: Compare the same type of apartment, location and holding period before deciding between buying and renting.
Include buying and selling expenses, annual ownership costs and the value of capital tied up in the property.
Test the answer against a shorter stay, different sale price, higher repairs and changes in rent.

sections.heading: Which cash flows should you compare?
sections.body:
For renting, include each year's rent, non-refundable agency and contract charges, moving costs and any utilities or insurance you would pay. A refundable deposit is cash you need at the start, but it is not necessarily an expense if it is returned in full. Record an expected deduction separately rather than assuming the whole deposit is lost.

For buying, include the agreed price, transaction costs, insurance, service charges, repairs and the eventual cost of sale. Subtract the actual net sale proceeds at the end of the period. If you borrow, distinguish interest and fees from repayment of principal: principal reduces the debt and normally contributes to your equity; it is not the same as an annual ownership expense.

Keep the buyer's capital visible. The renter may be able to use or invest the money that the buyer ties up in the apartment. Any assumed investment return carries its own risk and must be treated as an assumption, not a guaranteed benefit of renting.

sections.heading: A five-year illustration
sections.body:
Assume a renter pays AED 40,000 in the first year and, purely for the example, rent rises by 5% at each annual renewal. Five years of rent total about AED 221,025 before moving, contract and utility costs. The 5% is a scenario input; it is not a claim about a permitted increase or prevailing rents.

For the buying scenario, assume a cash price of AED 600,000, AED 25,000 in acquisition costs, AED 8,000 a year in ownership costs, a sale after five years for AED 600,000 and AED 18,000 in selling expenses. The simplified net cost is AED 625,000 plus AED 40,000 plus AED 18,000, less AED 600,000 in sale proceeds: AED 83,000.

The comparison deliberately excludes the opportunity cost of the buyer's capital, rent-side fees, major repairs, taxes that may apply to an individual's circumstances, and any change in the sale price. It is therefore a starting worksheet, not a recommendation or a forecast. The gap would narrow if the buyer's foregone return and other excluded costs were substantial.

chart.title: Five-year illustration before omitted costs
chart.note: The ownership figure assumes a cash purchase and resale at the same price. It excludes the return that capital might otherwise earn; both scenarios omit additional costs.

sections.heading: The length of stay can change the answer
sections.body:
A buyer incurs acquisition expenses at the beginning and may face selling expenses when leaving. Spread those costs over a short stay and they have a larger effect on the annual comparison. If a household might move within a year or two, compare the likely sale timetable, any early loan-settlement charge and the possibility that the property sells for less than the purchase price.

A longer stay gives more time to absorb one-off expenses but increases exposure to maintenance, building condition and household changes. Neither a long stay nor an attractive initial payment guarantees a profit. Run at least three exit scenarios: a lower sale price, the same price and a higher price. Use current comparable evidence to choose the assumptions and keep all three distinct from actual results.

If you expect to rent out the apartment after moving, do not treat that as an automatic exit. Estimate vacancy, management, service charges and repairs, and check the applicable tenancy process. Rental demand and the time needed to find a tenant can vary between buildings.

sections.heading: Check the real rent and the real unit
sections.body:
Compare the location, floor area, parking, building condition and included services. A cheap advertised rent for a different property type is not an equivalent alternative to the home you would buy. Ask for the actual annual rent, payment dates, commission, refundable deposit, any cooling or utility arrangements and renewal terms.

Ajman's [residential lease authentication service](https://ajman.ae/en/happiness-bundle/services/establish-business/authentication-lease-contract-residential-purposes) describes the Tasdeeq process and the documents and charges relevant to that service. Confirm the current requirements and fee allocation for the contract. Avoid assuming that a Dubai rental rule or a general online percentage applies to your Ajman tenancy.

For a purchase, obtain the [Ajman sale-registration requirements](https://www.ajman.ae/en/servicecatalog/services/3162), the developer's clearance when applicable and a unit-specific quote. The official English fee display needs clarification for some categories, so verify the amount directly before using it in a calculation.

sections.heading: How to stress-test the decision
sections.body:
Change one assumption at a time. First, calculate what happens if the buyer sells earlier and pays the same acquisition and sale costs over fewer years. Then test a lower resale value and an unplanned repair. For the rental case, use a different renewal quote and include an extra move. For finance, request a revised bank illustration for the rate after the introductory period.

Ask whether you can afford the worst realistic cash-flow year, not just whether the final five-year total is attractive. A household may have enough wealth overall but still be unable to pay a large handover instalment or unexpected repair on time. Conversely, an apartment with a predictable payment schedule may be useful for a buyer with a stable long-term plan.

Keep personal factors in the decision: the ability to relocate, permitted alterations, space for family, workplace changes and the time you are willing to spend managing a property. A spreadsheet cannot assign those values for you.

sections.heading: Compare current options before deciding
sections.body:
Use the [Ajman area guide](/journal/ajman-property-2026) to select locations, then review the [Aliyas Ajman project collection](/projects?emirate=Ajman) for homes that fit the same brief. Request the current availability and purchase terms for the apartment you are considering.

If you want help comparing the purchase side, [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your expected stay, budget, preferred areas and finance plans. Ask for written purchase and payment details, and obtain a current rental offer for a comparable apartment independently. Update the worksheet before an offer or lease commitment, because a change in price, fees or duration can alter the outcome.
